font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> </span></p><h2 dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.00in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; display: inline-block;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;text-indent: 0;width: 0.042in;"></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Opinion on the Consolidated Financial Statements</span></h2><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of CAI International, Inc.&#160;and subsidiaries (the Company) as of December&#160;31,&#160;2020 and 2019, the related consolidated statements of income, comprehensive income, stockholders&#8217; equity, and cash flows for each of the years in the three-year period ended December&#160;31,&#160;2020, and the related notes and financial statement schedule&#160;II (collectively, the consolidated financial statements).&#160;In our opinion, the consolidated financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Company as of December&#160;31,&#160;2020 and 2019, and the results of its operations and its cash flows for each of the years in the three-year period ended December&#160;31,&#160;2020, in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">We also have audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States) (PCAOB), the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting as of December&#160;31,&#160;2020, based on&#160;criteria established in </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Internal Control &#8211; Integrated Framework (2013)</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission, and our report dated March&#160;1,&#160;2021 expressed an unqualified opinion on the effectiveness of the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting.</span></p><h2 dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.00in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; display: inline-block;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;text-indent: 0;width: 0.042in;"></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Change in Accounting Principle</span></h2><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">As discussed in Note&#160;2 to the consolidated financial statements, the Company has changed its method of accounting for&#160;leases&#160;as of&#160;January 1, 2019 due to the adoption of Accounting Standards Codification Topic 842, </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Leases</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">.</span></p><h2 dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.00in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; display: inline-block;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;text-indent: 0;width: 0.042in;"></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Basis for Opinion</span></h2><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">These consolidated financial statements are the responsibility of the Company&#8217;s management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these consolidated financial statements based on our audits. We are a public accounting firm registered with the PCAOB and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the consolidated financial statements are free of material misstatement, whether due to error or fraud. Our audits included performing procedures to assess the risks of material misstatement of the consolidated financial statements, whether due to error or fraud, and performing procedures that respond to those risks. Such procedures included examining, on a test basis, evidence regarding the amounts and disclosures in the consolidated financial statements. Our audits also included evaluating the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall presentation of the consolidated financial statements. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</span></p><h2 dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.00in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; display: inline-block;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;text-indent: 0;width: 0.042in;"></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Critical Audit Matter</span></h2><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The critical audit matter communicated below is a matter arising from the current period audit of the consolidated financial statements that was communicated or required to be communicated to the audit committee and that: (1) relates to accounts or disclosures that are material to the consolidated financial statements and (2) involved our especially challenging, subjective, or complex judgments. The communication of a critical audit matter does not alter in any way our opinion on the consolidated financial statements, taken as a whole, and we are not, by communicating the critical audit matter below, providing a separate opinion on the critical audit matter or on the accounts or disclosures to which it relates.</span></p><h4 dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.00in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; display: inline-block;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;text-indent: 0;width: 0.042in;"></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Residual values of container rental equipment</span></h4><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">As discussed in Note&#160;5 to the consolidated financial statements, the net book value of container rental equipment as of December 31, 2020 was $1,781 million. Container rental equipment is recorded at cost and depreciated to an estimated residual value on a straight-line basis over its estimated useful lives. To determine the residual values of container rental equipment, the Company evaluates historical disposal experience and expectations for future used container sale prices.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">We identified the assessment of residual values of container rental equipment as a critical audit matter. Subjective auditor judgment was required given the significant measurement uncertainty of the residual values of container rental equipment. Specifically, subjective auditor judgment was required to evaluate the identification and evidence of trends affecting future used container sales prices.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"><br />&#8206;</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> </span></p></div>

    <div><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> </span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The following are the primary procedures we performed to address this critical audit matter. We evaluated the design and tested the operating effectiveness of certain internal controls over the Company&#8217;s residual value estimation process.&#160; This included controls over the methodology, which included the identification and assessment of trends affecting future used container sales prices. We tested historical and current year used container sales of the Company by examining a sample of sales invoices. We evaluated the Company&#8217;s methodology by comparing (1) trends identified in published industry reports to those identified by the Company within its historical data and (2) the estimated residual values of major equipment types to publicly available peer data. We assessed the mathematical accuracy of the Company&#8217;s model. We evaluated the residual values by comparing them to average selling prices of major equipment types of used containers for various historical periods.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;     <div><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies and Accounting Pronouncements</span></ix:nonNumeric></p><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-036a3fc4-0f36-46a1-9eca-0915d5befefd-continuation-0" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-036a3fc4-0f36-46a1-9eca-0915d5befefd-continuation-1"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 6pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-size: 6pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> </span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="ct-nonNumeric-fe977d22-4103-4757-b975-a11bb5ac3720" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2020_To_12_31_2020" escape="true" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-fe977d22-4103-4757-b975-a11bb5ac3720-continuation-0"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Recent Accounting Pronouncements</span></ix:nonNumeric></p><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-fe977d22-4103-4757-b975-a11bb5ac3720-continuation-0"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">In June 2016, the Financial&#160;Accounting&#160;Standards&#160;Board (FASB)&#160;issued Accounting&#160;Standards&#160;Update (ASU)&#160;No. 2016-13,&#160;</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Financial Instruments &#8211; Credit Losses (Topic 326)&#160;</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">(ASU 2016-13),&#160;and subsequently issued amendments. The guidance affects the Company&#8217;s net investment in finance leases, financing receivable and accounts receivable for sales of rental equipment. Topic 326 requires the measurement of expected credit losses to be based on relevant information from past events, including historical experiences, current conditions and reasonable and supportable forecasts that affect collectability. The Company adopted ASU 2016-13 effective January 1, 2020, using the modified retrospective method, which did not have a significant impact on the consolidated financial statements as credit losses are not expected to be significant based on historical loss trends, the financial conditions of customers, and expected external market factors.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The allowance for credit losses on net investment in finance leases and financing receivable is estimated on a collective basis by internal customer rating (see Note 6 &#8211; </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Leases</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> for descriptions of ratings). Expected credit losses for these financial assets are estimated using a loss-rate methodology which considers historical credit loss information that is adjusted for current conditions and reasonable and supportable forecasts.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Previously Adopted Accounting Pronouncements</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">In February 2016, the FASB issued ASU No. 2016-02, </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Leases (Topic 842) </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">(ASU 2016-02), and subsequently issued amendments thereto, that replaced existing lease accounting guidance. The new standard requires lessors to classify leases as a sales-type, direct financing, or operating lease. The new standard also established a right-of-use model (ROU) that requires lessees to recognize an ROU asset and lease liability on the balance sheet for all leases with a term longer than twelve months. The Company adopted ASU 2016-02, as amended, effective January 1, 2019, using the modified retrospective approach and the effective date as the date of initial application. Consequently, financial information has not been updated, and the disclosures required under the new standard have not been provided for dates and periods before January 1, 2019.</span></p></ix:continuation><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:ConsolidationPolicyTextBlock" id="ct-nonNumeric-de02cebf-6992-4406-8015-1732a2188450" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2020_To_12_31_2020" escape="true" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-de02cebf-6992-4406-8015-1732a2188450-continuation-0"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;">(a)   </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Principles of Consolidation</span></ix:nonNumeric></p><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-de02cebf-6992-4406-8015-1732a2188450-continuation-0" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-de02cebf-6992-4406-8015-1732a2188450-continuation-1"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The consolidated financial statements include the financial statements of CAI International, Inc. and its wholly-owned subsidiaries. All significant intercompany balances and transactions have been eliminated in consolidation. </span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The Company regularly performs a review of its container fund arrangements with investors to determine whether or not it has a variable interest in the fund and if the fund is a variable interest entity (VIE). If it is determined that the Company does not have a variable interest in the fund, further analysis is not required and the Company does not consolidate the fund. If it is determined that the Company does have a variable interest in the fund and the fund is a VIE, further analysis is performed to determine if the Company is a primary beneficiary of the VIE and meets both of the following criteria under </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">FASB Accounting Standards Codification (</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">ASC) Topic 810, </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Consolidation</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">:</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0.63in;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: -0.25in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;display: inline-block;font-family: Symbol;font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;text-indent: 0;width: 0.250in;">&#61623;</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">it has the power to direct the activities of the VIE that most significantly impact the VIE&#8217;s economic performance; and</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0.63in;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: -0.25in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;display: inline-block;font-family: Symbol;font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;text-indent: 0;width: 0.250in;">&#61623;</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">it has the obligation to absorb losses of the VIE that could be potentially significant to the VIE or the right to receive benefits from the VIE that could potentially be significant to the VIE.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">If in the Company&#8217;s judgment both of the above criteria are met, the VIE&#8217;s financial statements are included in the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements as required under FASB ASC Topic 810, </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Consolidation </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">(see Note 4).</span></p></ix:continuation></ix:continuation></div>

color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">On August 14, 2020, the Company sold substantially all of the assets and liabilities of its logistics business to NFI, a North American logistics provider, for cash proceeds of $</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"><ix:nonFraction id="ct-nonFraction-144c1f48-421c-45d1-bff7-134309a8daa5" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromDivestitureOfBusinesses" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2020_To_12_31_2020_us-gaap_IncomeStatementBalanceSheetAndAdditionalDisclosuresByDisposalGroupsIncludingDiscontinuedOperationsAxis_cai_LogisticsMember" unitRef="Unit1" decimals="-5" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="6">6.2</ix:nonFraction></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; On December 29, 2020, the Company sold its remaining railcar fleet to affiliates of Infinity Transportation for cash proceeds of $</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"><ix:nonFraction id="ct-nonFraction-1690b6da-c58b-4b97-a0ab-7963404e3547" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromDivestitureOfBusinesses" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2020_To_12_31_2020_us-gaap_IncomeStatementBalanceSheetAndAdditionalDisclosuresByDisposalGroupsIncludingDiscontinuedOperationsAxis_cai_RailcarAssetsMember" unitRef="Unit1" decimals="-5" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="6">228.1</ix:nonFraction></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> million. As a result, the operating results of the logistics and rail leasing businesses have been classified as discontinued operations in the accompanying consolidated statements of income and cash flows. All prior periods presented in these consolidated financial statements have been restated to reflect the classification of the logistics and rail leasing businesses as discontinued operations and certain assets and liabilities as held for sale. See Note 3 &#8211; </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Discontinued Operations </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">for more information.</span></p></ix:continuation><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:UseOfEstimates" id="ct-nonNumeric-0e50df5a-5785-4e5b-9b6b-4169964e462c" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2020_To_12_31_2020" escape="true" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-0e50df5a-5785-4e5b-9b6b-4169964e462c-continuation-0"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;">(c)   Use of Estimates</span></ix:nonNumeric></p><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-0e50df5a-5785-4e5b-9b6b-4169964e462c-continuation-0"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Certain estimates and assumptions were made by the Company&#8217;s management that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements and the reported amounts of revenue and expenses during the reporting periods. Significant items subject to such estimates and assumptions include revenue recognition, allowances for receivables, the carrying amount of rental equipment, the residual values and lives of rental equipment, and income tax uncertainties. Actual results could differ from those estimates.</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> </span></p></ix:continuation><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><ix:nonNumeric name="cai:RentalEquipmentPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="ct-nonNumeric-0fcaa971-2d4c-4e09-b24e-d58968b11235" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2020_To_12_31_2020" escape="true" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-0fcaa971-2d4c-4e09-b24e-d58968b11235-continuation-0"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;">(d)   Rental equipment</span></ix:nonNumeric></p><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-0fcaa971-2d4c-4e09-b24e-d58968b11235-continuation-0"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The Company purchases new container equipment from manufacturers to lease to its customers. The Company also purchases used container equipment through sale-leaseback transactions with its customers, or equipment that was previously owned by one of the Company&apos;s third-party investors. Used equipment is typically purchased with an existing lease in place. </span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Container rental equipment is recorded at original cost and depreciated to an estimated residual value on a straight-line basis over its estimated useful life. The estimated useful lives and residual values of the Company&#8217;s container equipment are based on historical disposal experience and the Company&#8217;s expectations for future used container sale prices. Depreciation estimates are reviewed on a regular basis to determine whether sustained changes have taken place in the useful lives of equipment or the assigned residual values, which would suggest that a change in depreciation estimates is warranted.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">For used container equipment acquired through sale-leaseback transactions, the Company often adjusts its estimates for remaining useful life and residual values based on current conditions in the sale market for older containers and its expectations for how long the equipment will remain on-hire to the current lessee.</span></p></ix:continuation><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOrDisposalOfLongLivedAssetsPolicyTextBlock" id="ct-nonNumeric-1c613e52-f637-4098-bcce-4c4efdc45278" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2020_To_12_31_2020" escape="true" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-1c613e52-f637-4098-bcce-4c4efdc45278-continuation-0"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;">(e)   Impairment of Long-Lived Assets</span></ix:nonNumeric></p><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-1c613e52-f637-4098-bcce-4c4efdc45278-continuation-0" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-1c613e52-f637-4098-bcce-4c4efdc45278-continuation-1"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">On at least an annual basis, the Company evaluates its rental equipment fleet to determine whether there have been any events or changes in circumstances indicating that the carrying amount of all, or part, of its fleet may not be recoverable. Events which would trigger an impairment review include, among others, a significant decrease in the long-term average market value of rental equipment, a significant decrease in the utilization rate of rental equipment resulting in an inability to generate income from operations and positive cash flow in future periods, or a change in market conditions resulting in a significant decrease in lease rates. </span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">When testing for impairment, equipment is generally grouped by equipment type, and is tested separately from other groups of assets and liabilities. Potential impairment exists when the estimated future undiscounted cash flows generated by an asset group, comprised of lease proceeds and residual values, less related operating expenses, are less than the carrying value of that asset group. If potential impairment exists, the equipment is written down to its fair value. In determining the fair value of an asset group, the Company considers market trends, published value for similar assets, recent transactions of similar assets and in certain cases, quotes from third party appraisers. </span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 1pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:FinanceLoansAndLeasesReceivablePolicy" id="ct-nonNumeric-25a4c2ae-51f0-454b-80ad-420988a58156" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2020_To_12_31_2020" escape="true" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-25a4c2ae-51f0-454b-80ad-420988a58156-continuation-0"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-size: 1pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> </span></ix:nonNumeric></p></ix:continuation></div></ix:continuation>

color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;">(h)   Derivative Instruments</span></ix:nonNumeric></p><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-3dd4f7c1-47e1-45c6-861b-cad5bc7c3b6d-continuation-0"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The Company enters into derivative agreements to manage interest rate risk exposure. Interest rate swap agreements are utilized to limit the Company&#8217;s exposure to interest rate risk by converting a portion of its floating-rate debt to fixed-rate basis, thus reducing the impact of interest rate changes on future interest expense. Interest rate swaps involve the receipt of floating-rate amounts in exchange for fixed rate interest payments over the lives of the agreements without an exchange of the underlying principal amounts. </span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The counterparties to these agreements are highly rated financial institutions. In the unlikely event that the counterparties fail to meet the terms of these agreements, the Company&#8217;s exposure is limited to the interest rate differential on the notional amount at each monthly settlement period over the life of the agreements. The Company does not anticipate any non-performance by the counterparties.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The Company records derivative instruments on its balance sheet at fair value and establishes criteria for both the designation and effectiveness of hedging activities. The fair value of the derivative instruments is measured at each balance sheet date and is reflected on a gross basis on the consolidated balance sheets. The change in fair value of the derivative instruments designated as cash flow hedges is recorded on the consolidated balance sheets in &#8216;Accumulated other comprehensive loss&#8217; and are reclassified to &#8216;Net interest expense&#8217; when realized. </span></p></ix:continuation><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> </span><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:ForeignCurrencyTransactionsAndTranslationsPolicyTextBlock" id="ct-nonNumeric-14b4fbee-20e9-4693-93d4-438b4e5c7cd0" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2020_To_12_31_2020" escape="true" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-14b4fbee-20e9-4693-93d4-438b4e5c7cd0-continuation-0"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;">(i)   Foreign Currency Translation</span></ix:nonNumeric></p><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-14b4fbee-20e9-4693-93d4-438b4e5c7cd0-continuation-0"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The accounts of the Company&#8217;s foreign subsidiaries have been converted at rates of exchange in effect at year-end for balance sheet accounts and average exchange rates for the year for income statement accounts. The effects of changes in exchange rates in translating foreign subsidiaries&#8217; financial statements are included in stockholders&#8217; equity as accumulated other comprehensive income.</span></p></ix:continuation><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:TradeAndOtherAccountsReceivablePolicy" id="ct-nonNumeric-a20bfa5c-3b58-43eb-ba43-9f151d9f024c" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2020_To_12_31_2020" escape="true" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-a20bfa5c-3b58-43eb-ba43-9f151d9f024c-continuation-0"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;">(j)   Accounts Receivable </span></ix:nonNumeric></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-a20bfa5c-3b58-43eb-ba43-9f151d9f024c-continuation-0"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Amounts billed under leases for equipment owned by the Company are recorded in accounts receivable. The Company estimates an allowance for doubtful accounts for accounts receivable it does not consider fully collectible. The allowance for doubtful accounts is developed based on two components: (1) specific reserves for receivables for which management believes full collection is doubtful; and (2) a general reserve for estimated losses inherent in the receivables. The general reserve is estimated by applying certain percentages to receivables that have not been specifically reserved, ranging from </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"><ix:nonFraction id="ct-nonFraction-2d337508-ccb8-4f12-813d-184dd376355d" name="cai:PercentageOfReserveOnReceivablesOverdueOneToThirtyDays" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2020_To_12_31_2020" unitRef="Unit13" decimals="3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="-2">1.0</ix:nonFraction></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; -sec-ix-hidden:ct-nonNumeric-31cbe156-2283-404c-8969-66d2ab94cdf5;">one</span></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> to </span><ix:nonNumeric name="cai:PeriodAccountsOverdueForGeneralReserveWithSpecificMinimumPercentage" id="ct-nonNumeric-86fba5ee-0141-46bd-ae7c-dee65df1d803" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2020_To_12_31_2020_srt_RangeAxis_srt_MaximumMember" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; The allowance for doubtful accounts is reviewed regularly by management and is based on the risk profile of the receivables, credit quality indicators such as the level of past due amounts and non-performing accounts and economic conditions. Changes in economic conditions or other events may necessitate additions or deductions to the allowance for doubtful accounts. The allowance is intended to provide for losses inherent in the company&#8217;s accounts receivable, and requires the application of estimates and judgments as to the outcome of collection efforts and the realization of collateral, among other things.</span></ix:continuation></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:LesseeLeasesPolicyTextBlock" id="ct-nonNumeric-2970248e-e7bc-49cc-acbd-ea9c65cbb849" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2020_To_12_31_2020" escape="true" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-2970248e-e7bc-49cc-acbd-ea9c65cbb849-continuation-0"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;">(k)   Leases</span></ix:nonNumeric></p><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-2970248e-e7bc-49cc-acbd-ea9c65cbb849-continuation-0"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The Company leases office space under operating leases with expiration dates through 2025. The Company determines&#160;whether an arrangement constitutes a lease and records lease liabilities and&#160;ROU&#160;assets on&#160;its&#160;consolidated balance sheet at lease commencement.&#160;Operating lease ROU assets and liabilities are recognized at commencement date based on the present value of lease payments over the lease term. As most of the Company&#8217;s leases do not provide an implicit rate, the Company uses its incremental borrowing rate based on the information available at commencement date in determining the present value of lease payments. The operating lease ROU assets also include any lease&#160;pre-payments made and exclude lease incentives. Certain of the Company&#8217;s leases include one or more options to renew, which are included in the lease term only when it is reasonably certain that the Company will exercise that option. The Company&#8217;s office space leases often include lease and non-lease components, which are combined and accounted for as a single lease component.&#160;</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">For short-term leases, the Company records rent expense in its consolidated statements of&#160;income&#160;on a straight-line basis over the lease term and records variable lease payments as incurred.&#160;</span></p></ix:continuation><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" id="ct-nonNumeric-f5bf4483-1c7c-4fc3-9930-6a763149db43" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2020_To_12_31_2020" escape="true" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-f5bf4483-1c7c-4fc3-9930-6a763149db43-continuation-0"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;"><br />&#8206;</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> </span></ix:nonNumeric></p></div></ix:continuation>
    <div><div class="footerContainer"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-align: center;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;" class="ctHeaderFooterPage">54</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; ct-page-break: true; page-break-after: always;" /><div class="headerContainer"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0.27in;margin-top: 0;"><a href="#TOC" style="text-decoration: none;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;">CAI INTERNATIONAL, INC.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0.27in;margin-top: 0;text-align: center;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;     <ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-036a3fc4-0f36-46a1-9eca-0915d5befefd-continuation-4" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-036a3fc4-0f36-46a1-9eca-0915d5befefd-continuation-5"><div><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-f5bf4483-1c7c-4fc3-9930-6a763149db43-continuation-0" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-f5bf4483-1c7c-4fc3-9930-6a763149db43-continuation-1"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> </span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;">(l)   Income Taxes</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Income taxes are accounted for using the asset-and-liability method. Under this method, deferred income taxes are recognized for the future tax consequences of differences between the tax bases of assets and liabilities and their financial reporting amounts at each year-end. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. Valuation allowances are established when it is more likely than not that deferred tax assets will not be recovered.</span></p></ix:continuation><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-f5bf4483-1c7c-4fc3-9930-6a763149db43-continuation-1"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The Company recognizes the effect of income tax positions only if those positions are more likely than not of being sustained. Recognized income tax positions are measured at the largest amount that is greater than 50% likely of being realized. Changes in recognition or measurement are reflected in the period in which the change in judgment occurs. The Company records penalties and interest related to unrecognized tax benefits within income tax expense (see Note 9).</span></ix:continuation></p><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:RevenueRecognitionPolicyTextBlock" id="ct-nonNumeric-b008e73a-c3a5-4d51-b0fe-eb2e1eaf0476" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2020_To_12_31_2020" escape="true" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-b008e73a-c3a5-4d51-b0fe-eb2e1eaf0476-continuation-0"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;">(m)   Revenue Recognition</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The Company provides a range of services to its customers incorporating the rental, sale and management of equipment. Revenue for all forms of service is recognized when earned following the guidelines under FASB ASC Topic 606, </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Revenue Recognition,</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> FASB ASC Topic 840,</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> Leases </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">and FASB ASC Topic 842, </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Leases</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">. Revenue is reported net of any related sales tax.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Container Lease Revenue</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The Company recognizes revenue from operating leases of its owned equipment as earned over the term of the lease. Where minimum lease payments vary over the lease term, revenue is recognized on a straight-line basis over the term of the lease. Early termination of the rental contracts subjects the lessee to a penalty, which is included in lease revenue upon such termination. Finance lease income, and interest earned on financing receivables are recognized using the effective interest method, which generates a constant rate of interest over the term of the arrangement.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Certain&#160;leases include one or more options to renew or purchase the leased rental equipment.&#160;The exercise of lease renewal or equipment purchase options is at the sole discretion of the customer.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Included in lease revenue is revenue consisting primarily of fees charged to the lessee for handling, delivery, and repairs. These&#160;activities&#160;are considered non-lease components of the contract, which are generally accounted for separately from the lease component, and revenue is recognized as earned&#160;in accordance with ASC&#160;Topic 606,&#160;</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Revenue Recognition</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">. &#160;</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Also included in lease revenue is revenue from management fees earned under equipment management agreements. Management fees are generally calculated as a percentage of the monthly net operating income for an investor&#8217;s portfolio and recognized as revenue in the month of service. </span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Unearned Revenue</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The Company records unearned revenue when cash payments are received in advance of the Company satisfying its performance obligations.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Payment terms vary by customer and type of service. The time between invoicing and when payment is due is not significant. For certain customers or services, the Company may require payment before the services are delivered or performed for the customer.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Practical Expedients</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The Company expenses sales commissions when incurred because the period of amortization would have been one year or less. These costs are recorded within administrative expenses.</span></p></ix:nonNumeric><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-b008e73a-c3a5-4d51-b0fe-eb2e1eaf0476-continuation-0"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The Company does not disclose the value of unsatisfied performance obligations for (i) contracts with an original expected length of one year or less and (ii) contracts with variable consideration for a distinct good or service that forms part of a single performance obligation.</span></ix:continuation></p><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationOptionAndIncentivePlansPolicy" id="ct-nonNumeric-647c77df-d28b-43dc-b30c-058a25c3e705" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2020_To_12_31_2020" escape="true" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-647c77df-d28b-43dc-b30c-058a25c3e705-continuation-0"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> (n)   Stock-Based Compensation</span></p></ix:nonNumeric><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-647c77df-d28b-43dc-b30c-058a25c3e705-continuation-0"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The Company has granted stock options, restricted stock awards, time-based restricted stock units and performance-based restricted stock units to certain directors and employees under its equity incentive plans. In addition, the Company operates an Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP). The Company accounts for stock-based compensation in accordance with FASB ASC Topic 718, </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Compensation &#8211; Stock Compensation</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">, which requires that compensation cost related to stock-based compensation be recognized in the financial statements.&#160;The cost is measured at the date the award is granted based on the fair value of the award. The fair value of stock options and shares purchased under the ESPP are calculated using the Black-Scholes-Merton option pricing model. The stock-based compensation expense is recognized over the vesting period of the grant on a straight-line basis (see Note 8). The Company accounts for forfeitures as they occur.</span></ix:continuation></p><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:MaintenanceCostPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="ct-nonNumeric-03e64b18-ddea-4dab-911e-887e9b1cb55d" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2020_To_12_31_2020" escape="true" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-03e64b18-ddea-4dab-911e-887e9b1cb55d-continuation-0"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;"><br />&#8206;</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> </span></p></ix:nonNumeric></div></ix:continuation>

    <div><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-d684f92a-01e6-4766-be17-67b9f74e4c69-continuation-1" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-d684f92a-01e6-4766-be17-67b9f74e4c69-continuation-2"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> </span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The terms of the transactions with container funds under financing arrangements include options for the Company to purchase the containers from the funds at a fixed price. As a result of the residual interest resulting from the fixed price call option, the Company concluded that it may absorb a significant amount of the variability associated with the funds&#8217; anticipated economic performance and, as a result, the Company has a variable interest in the funds. The funds are considered VIEs under FASB ASC Topic 810, </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Consolidation</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">, because, as lessee of the funds, the Company has the power to direct the activities that most significantly impact each entity&#8217;s economic performance, including the leasing and managing of containers owned by the funds. As the Company has the power to direct the activities that most significantly impact the economic performance of the VIEs and the variable interest provides the Company with the right to receive benefits from the entity that could potentially be significant to the funds, the Company determined that it is the primary beneficiary of these VIEs and included the VIEs&#8217; assets and liabilities as of December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019, and the results of the VIEs&#8217; operations and cash flows for the years ended December&#160;31, 2020, 2019 and 2018 in the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements.</span></p></ix:continuation><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-d684f92a-01e6-4766-be17-67b9f74e4c69-continuation-2"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The containers that were transferred to the Japanese investor funds had a net book value of $</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"><ix:nonFraction id="ct-nonFraction-b15c42e3-4745-4481-a323-945490bd4125" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentOtherNet" contextRef="As_Of_12_31_2020_srt_ConsolidatedEntitiesAxis_us-gaap_VariableInterestEntityPrimaryBeneficiaryMember_us-gaap_PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis_us-gaap_ContainersMember" unitRef="Unit1" decimals="-5" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="6">80.6</ix:nonFraction></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">&#160;million as of December&#160;31, 2020. color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Credit quality information</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">In order to estimate the allowance for losses contained in net investment in finance leases and financing receivable, the Company reviews the credit worthiness of its customers on an ongoing basis. The review includes monitoring credit quality indicators, historical credit loss activity, current market and economic conditions, and reasonable and supportable forecasts.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The Company uses the following definitions for risk ratings:</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Tier 1</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">&#8212; These customers are typically large international shipping lines that have been in business for many years and have world-class operating capabilities and significant financial resources. In most cases, the Company has had a long commercial relationship with these customers and currently maintains regular communication with them at several levels of management, which provides the Company with insight into the customer&apos;s current operating and financial performance. In the Company&apos;s view, these customers have the greatest ability to withstand cyclical down turns and would likely have greater access to needed capital than lower-rated customers. The Company views the risk of default for Tier 1 customers to range from minimal to moderate.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Tier 2</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">&#8212; These customers are typically either smaller shipping lines or freight forwarders with less operating scale or with a high degree of financial leverage, and accordingly the Company views these customers as subject to higher volatility in financial performance over the business cycle. The Company generally expects these customers to have less access to capital markets or other sources of financing during cyclical down turns. The Company views the risk of default for Tier 2 customers as moderate.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: 0.38in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; and</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 6pt;margin-left: 0.75in;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: -0.25in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap;
